response.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT o.timespan, AVG(f.rebrate / NULLIF(f.feerate, 0)) AS avg_ratio, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.timespan), k AS (SELECT timespan, avg_ratio, cnt, AVG(cnt) OVER () AS avg_cnt FROM g) SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS avg_of_avg_ratios, SUM(cnt) AS total_fee_records, AVG(cnt - avg_cnt) AS avg_excess_over_mean_count FROM k WHERE cnt > avg_cnt

assumptions.assumption: The ratio is computed per fee record as rebrate / feerate. A feerate of 0 gives a NULL ratio (via NULLIF), so it is ignored in the average like other missing values. The fee record still counts toward the group's count.
Fee-record count is COUNT(*) of joined rows, including rows whose ratio is NULL. The cross-group average count is the unweighted mean of the per-group counts.
Any fees whose order has a NULL timespan form their own group, which is included in the cross-group average. It is also eligible to be kept.
